verdict.rationale: GitCafe documents a REST API described in OpenAPI 3.1, with idempotent `requestId` retries. Personal access tokens grant scripts the same permissions as the user. The `cafe` CLI manages repositories, pull requests, stacks, issues and more, offers `--json` output, and can send authenticated calls to any REST endpoint; an MCP server also exposes issue and PR work to agents. The core of programmatic access is clearly there, but no source explicitly claims full UI/API parity. The probe found none of the standard OpenAPI paths, which suggests the spec is hosted elsewhere rather than contradicting the docs. Missing for 10: an explicit statement or coverage map showing every UI action (e.g. rulesets, CI tab, sync settings) has an API equivalent, a publicly reachable OpenAPI spec, and independent hands-on corroboration.
